edges.description: The Sylamer analysis of the diminuendo organ of Corti is the primary evidence that a mutant miR-96 seed acquires targets, and it is the only place both halves of the mechanism have been shown in the same tissue.
edges.limitations: The seed position mutated in diminuendo is not one of the two positions mutated in human DFNA50 families, so the specific set of acquired targets is allele-specific and need not match a human carrier's. Enrichment of mutant-seed matches in human and rat orthologues of the downregulated genes was reported as barely above the significance threshold, unlike the wild-type-seed signal, so the acquired target set is the less conserved half of the mechanism.

edges.description: Single hair cell electrophysiology in this mutant is what established that the cellular lesion is arrested maturation at around the day of birth rather than degeneration of a differentiated cell.
edges.limitations: The arrest was characterised in neonatal mice; the corresponding human onset is postlingual, so the developmental timing of the mouse lesion is much earlier than the clinical presentation it is taken to explain. Homozygous mice, in which the arrest is complete, have no human counterpart - no homozygous DFNA50 patient has been reported.

edges.description: Heterozygous carriers of the human allele show the same failure of outer hair cell bundle maturation - a U rather than a V - seen in diminuendo, on a genotype that is an exact match for a human patient.
edges.limitations: Bundle scoring was qualitative rather than a quantified morphometric, and the genotype was assessed on a single inbred background, C57BL/6N, which carries its own age-related hearing loss allele. The paired +13G>A line shows how much background and allele interact: the same experiment on a mixed background changed nothing for that allele, but the possibility that background modifies the +14C>A bundle phenotype was not tested.

edges.description: Heterozygotes lose hearing progressively from four weeks, starting at high frequencies and spreading, which is the same shape of course as the human disease.
edges.limitations: The mouse course runs over weeks and the human course over decades, so the model compresses the natural history rather than reproducing its timescale. Homozygotes, profoundly deaf from four weeks, have no human counterpart.

edges.description: Two independent preclinical rescue arms have been run in this line. AAV delivery of SaCas9-KKH with a guide RNA against the mutant allele into the cochleae of presymptomatic and symptomatic adult mice improved hearing long term, with better results from earlier injection. Separately, amitriptyline - selected by matching the mutant transcriptome against anti-correlated drug expression profiles - delayed progression at high frequencies.
edges.limitations: Neither arm is a treatment. Editing disrupts the mutant allele rather than correcting it, was delivered directly into the cochlea, and the reported long-term benefit is preservation and partial improvement rather than normal hearing. The amitriptyline effect is temporary, was obtained at doses far above human therapeutic exposure by body weight, and did not benefit homozygotes or improve when the dose was doubled; the authors state explicitly that it is a proof of concept and not a proposed human treatment. Neither has been tested in a person.

edges.description: In heterozygosis - the genotype a human patient has - this model does not reproduce the disease. ABR thresholds stay normal to one year, and neither a different genetic background nor noise exposure unmasked a phenotype.
edges.limitations: This is the model's defining limitation and the reason it cannot be used to argue about human +13G>A carriers. The failure is genotype-specific rather than total: the homozygote is profoundly deaf and the line remains informative for the synaptic lesion and for the transcriptomic comparison against +14C>A. Whether the discrepancy reflects a species difference in the acquired target set, a threshold effect, or mouse lifespan being too short for a slowly progressive human phenotype has not been resolved.

edges.description: The line does reproduce a hair cell programme shift, but a different one from its sibling: the dominant lesion is a reduction in inner hair cell ribbon synapses rather than stereociliary bundle disruption, and the two mutants' differentially expressed gene sets are notably dissimilar.
edges.limitations: Only the homozygote shows the synaptic deficit, so the finding does not describe the genotype human patients carry. Because the two knock-in lines diverge this much, a programme change measured in this line cannot be assumed to hold for +14C>A or for the diminuendo allele.
edges.target: Dysregulation of the Hair Cell Maturation Gene Programme

edges.description: A null allele cannot acquire targets, so this model reproduces only the abandoned half of the mechanism. That is precisely its value: because null heterozygotes hear normally while seed-mutant heterozygotes do not, the dominant phenotype cannot be explained by loss of normal targeting alone.
edges.limitations: The deletion removes Mir183 as well as Mir96, so a comparison against a seed mutant confounds the two microRNAs; and the transcriptomes were compared across studies rather than in one experiment. The conclusion is an inference from a phenotype and transcriptome contrast, not a direct demonstration that any particular acquired target drives the disease.

nodes.description: Sensory hair cells stop developing around the day of birth, before inner and outer hair cells have diverged into their distinct biophysical identities. This is the central cellular lesion of the disease and it is a failure to finish maturing, not injury to a finished cell.

evidence.reference_title: miR-96 regulates the progression of differentiation in mammalian cochlear inner and outer hair cells.
evidence.snippet: We found that the physiological development of mutant sensory hair cells is arrested at around the day of birth, before their biophysical differentiation into inner and outer hair cells.

nodes.description: The two target-repertoire changes converge on a hair cell transcriptome that is shifted rather than simply damaged. In the diminuendo organ of Corti 96 transcripts are significantly altered, and the striking finding is which ones fall: Slc26a5 (prestin), Ocm (oncomodulin), Gfi1, Ptprq and Pitpnm1, all required for hair cell maturation or function and none of them carrying a predicted miR-96 site. Their downregulation is therefore a network consequence, not direct de-repression, and it is specific to this mutant - the same genes stain normally in nine other mouse mutants with early hair cell degeneration.

evidence.snippet: The reduction in Ptprq observed in diminuendo mice appears to be a major contributor to the morphological, transcriptional and electrophysiological phenotype, but does not account for the complete diminuendo phenotype.

nodes.description: Active amplification by outer hair cells fails, from two directions: prestin, the motor protein that drives outer hair cell length changes, is among the most downregulated transcripts, and the outer hair cells that carry it degenerate. The endocochlear potential is normal, so this is a sensory-cell failure and not a stria vascularis or ionic-homeostasis failure - a useful discriminator against the other routes into the sensorineural hair cell loss module.

nodes.description: Transcripts that carry a wild-type miR-96 site are no longer repressed and their levels rise. In the diminuendo organ of Corti the heptamer complementary to the wild-type seed is enriched in the 3-prime UTRs of hundreds of upregulated genes, and the same wild-type sites are enriched in the human and rat orthologues of those genes, so the target set is conserved rather than a mouse peculiarity. The quantitative reading is appropriate here: silencing of this particular target set is reduced, not qualitatively redirected, which is why the modifier is DECREASED.

nodes.description: The third human allele, found in one Italian family, is not a seed mutation. It lies outside the mature miR-96 sequence, in the companion miR-96* strand of the precursor hairpin, and destabilises the hairpin so that Dicer cleavage is impaired. Mature miR-96 and miR-96* both fall while the precursor itself does not accumulate less, and a compensatory second mutation that restores hairpin pairing restores their levels. Because the mature seed is unchanged, this allele can only reduce repression of the normal target set; it cannot acquire novel targets. It is included as a separate initiating node for exactly that reason.

evidence.snippet: Although located outside the mature miR-96 sequence, the detected variant replaces a highly conserved nucleotide within the companion miR-96*, and is predicted to reduce the stability of the pre-miRNA hairpin.

genetic_context.description: Unlike the seed alleles, this one has a controlled value that fits: the defect is purely quantitative, a reduced yield of an otherwise normal mature miR-96, which is what PARTIAL_LOSS_OF_FUNCTION describes.

nodes.description: A single-nucleotide substitution inside the seed of mature miR-96. Two such alleles are known in humans, +13G>A and +14C>A, each segregating in one Spanish family; the ENU-derived mouse allele diminuendo is a third, at a neighbouring seed position. The seed is nucleotides 2 to 7 of the mature strand and is what selects the target set, so a substitution there changes which transcripts miR-96 recognises rather than how much miR-96 there is - although mature-miRNA abundance is reduced as well.

nodes.description: Not a model of DFNA50 but the control that defines it. Deleting the microRNAs outright gives normal hearing in heterozygotes and complete deafness in homozygotes, and produces fewer transcriptional changes than the seed point mutant does. It is the experiment that separates absence of miR-96 from presence of a mutant miR-96.

A knock-in of the other human seed allele, from Spanish family s403. Homozygotes are profoundly deaf, but heterozygotes hear normally to a year old - the opposite of the human family, where the same heterozygous allele causes progressive hearing loss. The line also shows a distinct lesion from its +14C>A sibling: fewer inner hair cell ribbon synapses rather than a severe bundle phenotype.

A knock-in of the actual human +14C>A allele from Spanish family s1334, and the model that most closely matches human DFNA50: heterozygotes develop progressive hearing loss from four weeks with rounded outer hair cell bundles, and homozygotes are profoundly deaf. It is also the model used for the gene-editing and drug-repurposing experiments.

Outer hair cells in the middle and basal turns degenerate while most inner hair cells survive. The ordering matters for how the disease should be read: hearing loss is already severe while many hair cells are still present, so degeneration follows the dysfunction rather than causing it.

nodes.description: The mutant seed is complementary to a different heptamer, so transcripts carrying that motif - which the wild-type miRNA ignored - are now repressed. The signature is visible in the same diminuendo transcriptome that shows the loss of normal targeting: the mutant seed match is enriched among the most downregulated genes. This is the half of the mechanism that a null allele cannot reproduce, and it is why null heterozygotes hear while seed-mutant heterozygotes do not.

nodes.description: The stereociliary bundle does not acquire its mature form. In diminuendo heterozygotes outer hair cell bundles form a loose U rather than the precise V of controls, and inner hair cell bundles are smaller and more widely separated; homozygotes have irregular bundles and persistent clusters of ectopic stereocilia. The same rounding of the outer hair cell V is seen in mice carrying the human +14C>A allele. Bundle maturation and the remodelling of auditory nerve connections both fail.

nodes.description: The founding animal model and the one that supplied the mechanism. Heterozygotes lose the Preyer reflex between four and six weeks and have thresholds raised by about 60 dB; homozygotes have no cochlear responses. The allele is not one of the two human alleles - it is a third seed position - but it is the model in which the loss of normal targeting and the gain of novel targeting were both demonstrated in one transcriptome.
